newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea names new vice defence minister.
newsitem.headline: North Korea names new vice defence minister.

text.p: North Korea has appointed Vice Marshal Kim Il-chol as a new first vice defence minister, a post left vacant by the death of Kim Kwang-jin in February, a senior South Korean government official said on Monday.
But the Stalinist state has yet to appoint a defence minister to succeed Choe Kwang, who also died in February, said Park Sung-hoon, a director-general at the National Unification Ministry.
Park said Kim Il-chol was one of four generals promoted to vice marshal on Sunday.

"In a broadcast on Sunday Kim Il-chol was confirmed to have been appointed as the first vice defence minister," Park told Reuters. "It is yet another sign that Kim Jong-il is consolidating his grip on power."

He said Kim Il-chol was the most senior military officer among 123 generals North Korean leader Kim Jong-il promoted on Sunday. It was the biggest-scale promotion announced by North Korea since the death of former President Kim Il-sung in 1994.
"All the 123 officers are those trusted by Kim Jong-il," he said.
Park said the promotions appeared to be timed to mark the birthday on Tuesday of Kim Il-sung, the founder of the Stalinist state who named his son Jong-il as his heir before his death.
Earlier on Monday, Tokyo-based Radiopress news agency quoted Pyongyang's Korea Central Radio as saying a total of 122 army officers were promoted, but Park said the number was 123.

Kim Jong-il, supreme commander of the country's 1.1-million-strong military, has yet to be formally confirmed in two key posts held by his late father -- general secretary of the ruling Workers' Party and state president.
North Korea watchers believe Kim Jong-il is likely to formally assume the posts this year after the third anniversary of his father's death in July.
